scope: Follow-up to the completed initial national discovery pass and the 1,121 recorded regional searches. This is not another discovery sweep or a claim of an exhaustive regional inventory.
method: Official legal and institutional evidence; normal Chromium page navigation for the four held candidates. Search-index access is distinguished from direct page access. Eligibility is an editorial application of project scope, not a claim that excluded bodies have no public powers.

authority_reviews.candidate_action: Reject sweden-skane for catalogue scope; retain the evidence, independently of HTTP 403.

evidence.finding: Elected regional council controls healthcare, transport, regional development, culture, budgets and regional tax.
Instrument of Government chapters 8 and 14 distinguish Acts of the Riksdag, delegated provisions and elected local-authority decision making.
Local Government Act chapter 5 section 1 governs council goals, budget, tax, organisation and accountability; future commencement clauses must be considered separately.

authority_reviews.assessment: The documented role fits the project's regional service/local-government exclusion. Taxation, elections and executive scrutiny do not alone establish the required legislative status. This is a catalogue decision, not a denial of local self-government or delegated regulation.
authority_reviews.remaining: Reconsider only if specific legislative-status evidence or the project's scope changes.

authority_reviews.candidate_action: Authority gate passes; broadcast-service promotion remains separate.

evidence.finding: Parliament makes cantonal laws and decrees, approves the budget and supervises government, administration and the management of higher courts.

authority_reviews.assessment: Cantonal legislature with substantive law-making, finance and oversight powers. The name Grand Council is not a reason to exclude it.
authority_reviews.remaining: Resolve a current public session/archive landing page, identity, source conditions and accessibility. The indexed video test page is a lead, not a production-service validation.

authority_reviews.candidate_action: Retain existing catalogue records; do not expand all 47 prefectures on the basis of the assembly name.

evidence.finding: Assembly adopts, amends and repeals prefectural ordinances, decides budgets, consents to important appointments and investigates executive administration.
Articles 2 and 3 describe the assembly's independent representative, decision-making, scrutiny and policy roles.

evidence.method: official constitutional translation surfaced in search
evidence.finding: Constitution article 94 protects local entities' administration and enactment of regulations within law.

authority_reviews.assessment: There are real ordinance-making and executive-scrutiny powers. Calling these merely a service board would be inaccurate. The unresolved catalogue question is whether this constitutionally protected local legislative model qualifies under the agreed distinction from ordinary local councils; neither first-level status nor the English word assembly settles it.
authority_reviews.remaining: Compare the scope of autonomous prefectural ordinances and sanctions with municipal powers under the current Local Autonomy Act, then record a consistent scope decision. No removal or eligibility assertion is made in this pass.

authority_reviews.candidate_action: Retain all twelve as held; do not apply this assessment to Aruba, Curaçao, Sint Maarten or Caribbean island councils.

evidence.method: opened official English constitutional translation, 2018 edition
evidence.finding: Articles 124 and 127 establish provincial internal-affairs regulation and council enactment of ordinances, alongside municipal provisions; this is not a current consolidated statute check.

evidence.method: official government guidance surfaced in search
evidence.finding: Provincial councils hold a separate provincial executive accountable.

evidence.method: direct access failed (429/robots); official search-index excerpts available
evidence.finding: Indexed Provinciewet articles 143 and 145 describe council ordinances, including those judged necessary in provincial interests. Do not treat a dated indexed consolidation as verified current law.

authority_reviews.assessment: Provincial ordinance authority includes an autonomous component; it must not be described as exclusively delegated national administration. A title-based exclusion is as unsupported as automatic inclusion.
authority_reviews.remaining: Read a current accessible official consolidation and compare autonomous rule-making with the local-government exclusion. The twelve province rows remain held; constituent-country parliaments retain separate decisions.
